title: Building PHP CLI Applications
keywords: cli tools, background jobs, and automation
learning_outcomes: Explain what building php cli applications contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: script arguments.

content.intro: CLI scripts and background jobs need explicit inputs, predictable exit behavior, bounded resource use, observable failures, and safe retry semantics. Long-running work should not rely on a browser request staying open. In this lesson, focus on script arguments; then compare it with standard input. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use building php cli applications when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
